status: GAME BALANCE. Tunable gameplay values for simcore/engagement.hpp. These are not performance data for any real system; only the values whose 'source' names a document come from one, and those only set when lamps light.
notes: Change these to tune difficulty. The debrief prints every factor that went into each hit or miss, so the effect of a change is visible.

zone.source: max range, altitude limits: SAM Simulator Osa-AK manual p9, p14; warning time: p29 (ВНИМАНИЕ 15 s ahead). min_range_m is a game value.
zone.notes: Used for the ЦЕЛЬ В ЗОНЕ and ВНИМАНИЕ lamps and the outcome's zone factor.

zones.source: flak11 (Osa-AK engagement zones: head-on 1.5-10 km, 25-5000 m at up to 300 m/s and 100-5000 m at up to 500 m/s; pursuit to 6.5 km, 100-5000 m, up to 300 m/s; optical 'F' zone for targets at up to 100 m/s or hovering, 2-6.5 km, 10-25 m); docs/research/OSA_RESEARCH_2026-10.md section 5.
zones.notes: The head-on range limits are the 'zone' box above (1.5-10.3 km: the SAM Simulator manual's 10.3 km against the NVA's 10 km; the manual's was kept). The NVA's 'parameter' limit (6 km / 4 km of crossing offset) is not modelled. A target is 'approaching' when its closing speed is positive; otherwise it is in the pursuit zone or outside.

tv.source: reticle_deg: ePap (samsim_thread): the TV sight is tracked by hand with a 3-mil reticle, 3 thousandths on the 6000-division circle = 0.18 degrees; memory_s follows ePap's memory mode (it carries on at the last angular rates when the target is masked). The rest are game values.
tv.notes: Manual TV tracking. The TV channel follows the wheels: the target has to stay in the lens field (data/procedures/osa_ak.json, sensors.track.fov_deg) around where the azimuth and elevation wheels point, or the track is lost. An NPC in a wheel's seat follows the target npc_delay_s behind it and no faster than the aim rates; the player turns the wheels. The mean distance of the target from the crosshair during a missile's flight costs hit chance: factor = max(error_factor_min, 1 - error_penalty_per_reticle x mean error / reticle). Without this group the servo drives the wheels onto the target by itself once the TV has locked.

methods.source: samsim_thread (creator, ePap: T/T above elevation 00-30, the 'Gorka' zoom climb or 'F' for low targets); korovin_tiv_2010 (Gorka against targets at 50-100 m, so the fuse is not set off by the ground).
methods.notes: 00-30 is 30 thousandths on the Soviet 6000-division circle: 1.8 degrees. The method is printed in the debrief and decides nothing else: its effect is in outcome.low_altitude. 'N' (no range, against jammers) is not modelled.

search.notes: Game value: with СДЦ (MTI) off, targets below this height are lost in ground clutter.

track.source: range_gate_m: half the 1.5 km magnified sweep, SAM Simulator Osa-AK manual p24. The rest are game values; clutter_altitude_m rests on the SSC range channel sharing the MTI canceller (mon_2112_80 p15, p23) and is an estimate.
track.notes: How close the operator must set the azimuth line and range gate for ЦУ АЗ to capture; below min_altitude_m the radar can't hold angles (НЛЦ) and the TV must be used; below clutter_altitude_m it can't hold the target in the ground clutter unless the operator has СДЦ on (ssc.mti). em_capture_*: with the EM layer the auto-capture circuit takes the lock once the tracking radar has echoed on 22 of its last 40 looks (4 s; a local Pd of about 0.55). A raw lock starts on a lucky echo far out where Swerling I detection is still a few tenths (27 km for a 3 m2 target at 5 km altitude); this rule is tied to the one fitted calibration (Korovin's 23 km at 5 km altitude, Pd 0.5): it captures that target at 21 to 25 km. Raising the Pd does not help his 14 km at 50 m (the full-path Pd of a 50 m target is smooth: 0.5 at 22 km, 0.8 at 18 km). A model choice, not a published figure.

aim.notes: Roles: who turns each wheel (flak11, 9A33-3); they are console stations. The rest are game values: how fast an NPC turns each wheel onto a contact. plotting_board_range_m: the PU-12 board is watched from 50 km (manual p21).

missile.notes: Game pacing only: the delay between launch and result is range / average_speed. max_flight_time_s follows the manual's 24–27 s (p27).

outcome.source: low_altitude is calibrated to the published single-missile kill probabilities (docs/research/OSA_RESEARCH_2026-10.md section 5): flak11 (strike aircraft at 10 m 0.12-0.55, helicopters at 10 m 0.07-0.12, cruise missiles at 10 m 0.12-0.38) and korovin_tiv_2010 (0.35-0.4 at 50 m, 0.42-0.85 above 100 m, original 9K33 against an F-4C). With the class chances above this gives a fighter 0.39 at 50 m, a bomber 0.32 and a helicopter 0.10 at 10 m. Everything else here is a game value.
outcome.notes: Game values. chance = hit_chance[class] x (TV track ? tv_factor : 1) x (in zone at launch ? 1 : outside_zone_factor) x max(manoeuvre_factor_min, 1 - penalty x target turn rate in deg/s) x max(deviation_factor_min, 1 - deviation_penalty x crew mistakes) x low_altitude[class](height of the target above the ground at impact), linear between the points, flat beyond them.
